name: msync
synopsis: int msync(void *addr, size_t length, int flags);
description: msync() flushes changes made to a memory-mapped file back to the filesystem, ensuring that modifications are written from memory to disk. It synchronizes the specified memory range corresponding to the file.

parameters.name: addr
parameters.description: Starting address of the memory region to synchronize

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Length of the memory region in bytes

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags specifying synchronization behavior, such as MS_ASYNC, MS_SYNC, or MS_INVALIDATE

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: MS_INVALIDATE was specified and a memory lock exists for the address range
addr is not a multiple of PAGESIZE, invalid flags, or both MS_SYNC and MS_ASYNC are set
The indicated memory (or part of it) was not mapped

versions: Introduced in Linux 1.3.21; changes in Linux 2.4.19 and 2.6.19
